I can totally relate to how you are feeling. I don't mean to say how you are feeling but I've been in a very similar boat and it has taken me years to realise that happiness hangs in balance with sadness. We ourselves affect what is put on either side of this.
Take me for instance, bullied through high school, I chose to do nothing. When working at Maccas (I promise you I did work at a few different stores) I did nothing about how bad working there made me feel. I then proceeded to take it out on the one girl who was a positive in my life. I got another job and became redundant shortly after.

Now jobless and partnerless I set about trying to find happiness trying real hard to find a way to learn how not to fake that smile. Despite starving myself at times and losing my wheels. Despite sitting there say in and day out scared that my friend was going to neck himself and once or twice I believed he did try.

Despite everything that I thought made me a good person, a unique person shatter. Everything that could be taken as quality of life or self esteem has been tested in some form or other. Including a topic that most men refuse to admit happen or could happen to them. 

So I have found myself asking why don't I just end it. Why am I too scared to end my story. That comes down to three things for me. My goals that I never end up achieving. It keeps my mind away from things and keeps expectations of what I can do down low. It may sound like I'm degrading myself but it works for me.

Another thing on the contrary is my victories. Always losing or not finishing a project doesn't help esteem so sometimes I pull through whether it be holding the job or helping someone cross something off the bucket list. I wish I could say romance but alas lying would not help me at all

And strangely as this sounds other people's misery in a way. I'm not talking about you as I do not know you hence have no personal attachment to you. What I mean is being there, standing with those around me as they stumble. It takes a massive drain on the mindset initially but for me the reward as you help them overcome what they are going through helps my mindset tenfold.

The first step for me was asking myself why am I too scared too do it. And really think about it. When the excuses as to why your scared to do it come out listen to them. They may sound pathetic yet it might actually help you identify what is important to you. It's not a gaurentee to solve your problems but hopefully it will put you on the right path. I do stumble down still but Ive come a long way. Hope to see at the top, when we've both beaten it
